_comment: THE STORES THE FACTORY IS HELD AGAINST, and every one of them is a real
request from the Issues tab rather than a site chosen because it works.
That is the whole point: a suite built from stores that already pass
proves nothing, and until 22 September 2026 every fault in this factory
was found by a colleague pasting a URL rather than by anything here.
factory/soak.mjs reads this list, runs the READ HALF against each one and
reports what a demo built from it would contain. It makes no demo and
expect is what a good build looks like for that store, recorded the first
time it was seen. A store that drops below it has regressed, and the
report says so rather than leaving somebody to compare by eye. A store
with no expect block is being watched rather than judged.
A STORE THAT CANNOT BE READ STAYS ON THIS LIST. vperfumes and
mercadolivre are here because they are hard, not despite it: the answer
for a store behind a bot wall is a clean refusal and a request for a CSV,
and that path deserves testing as much as the happy one.

EXPECT IS TODAY, NOT THE TARGET. Each block is what that store actually gave on 22 September 2026, so a drop is a regression in this repository. Two stores have no expect block because they currently produce a demo with no navigable shelves at all, and recording that as acceptable would be writing a fault down as a standard. Their notes say so instead.

THE THEME IS WATCHED, NOT JUDGED, and the reason is in the numbers: the same store gave two different primaries on two runs an hour apart. That is worth knowing and is not yet worth failing a night over, so the soak reports the colour and the typeface it read and holds nobody to them.

A BASELINE IS ONLY WORTH WHAT THE MACHINE THAT RUNS IT CAN READ. factory/checks/drill-sites.txt has said since August that an address earns its place by reading from a GitHub runner rather than from a developer machine, because the two answers genuinely differ, and the first baselines here were recorded from a container instead. The first nightly run refused four Shopify stores that read perfectly from that container. Any expect block below is therefore provisional until a run from the runner confirms it, and a store that cannot be read from there belongs in the watch list with no expect block rather than failing every night.

stores.note: Shopify, typing beats its own collections
VTEX, but reads through jsonld from some networks: the tier is not stable
VTEX, serves runners a challenge page
Shopify, product_type empty; one shelf from its collections, most of the catalogue still in the tail

NO SHELVES. Its category grids are rendered in the browser, so the markup walk finds nothing; the browser pass now runs over them and still matches none of the products this build read, so the two are keyed differently. Unsolved on 22 September 2026.
NO SHELVES. Its sitemap index lists Arabic sitemaps only and its category pages live outside /collections/, so the walk has nothing to read. Unsolved on 22 September 2026.
